clue.text: Attack garden pest with empty skillet

parts.note: moles dig up lawns and are a gardener's pest

indicators.note: an empty word has had its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the word's outer letters once it is hollowed out

explanation.surface: Someone goes after a garden pest armed with an empty frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest is an old sense of to assail or harass, which fits attack as a verb.

clue.text: Manipulate crowd, given time

indicators.note: one thing given another has it attached, so the two pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A demagogue works on a crowd once he has had time to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulate' reads as a political sneer, but here it means rubbing and kneading muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: To massage is to knead the body with the hands, the physical sense of manipulate.

clue.text: Newly formed petal sprang forth

indicators.note: something newly formed has been made over, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh petal bursts out of a bud in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, to jump, which matches sprang forth in tense and meaning.

clue.text: Display reined in by weapon is bloody, possibly

indicators.note: something reined in is held back inside a restraint, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a sword is a bladed weapon
to wear something, such as a badge, is to display it

explanation.surface: A show of restraint around a weapon turns out to be bloody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a description of the weapon, but it is a mild British oath, and 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloody is a common British expletive, so it is an example of an obscenity or curse.

clue.text: Lips coated with Tory colour

indicators.note: a thing coated with something is wrapped in it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories
the lip of a cup or bowl is its rim

explanation.surface: A Conservative's lips are painted in the party's colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tory colour is blue, which tempts the solver away from red; the colour here is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red, so it is one example of a colour.

clue.text: Flower found in bad tempered woman's border

parts.note: cow is a rude word for an unpleasant woman; the possessive adds S
a lip is the edge or rim of something

explanation.surface: A flower grows in the border of a grumpy woman's garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow wild primula, a spring flower of British meadows.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing violinist ignoring first and third parts

indicators.note: ignoring parts means leaving out the letters in the first and third positions of the word

parts.note: a fiddler plays the fiddle, an informal name for the violin

explanation.surface: A useless violinist skips the first and third movements of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the F and the first D from FIDDLER to leave IDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who avoids work, which is what a good-for-nothing is.

clue.text: Inflexible length of twine ruined net

parts.note: a piece of twine is a string

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rigid piece of twine has wrecked a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and do not bend, the figurative sense of unbending or inflexible.

clue.text: German embraced by naked daughter is gently prodded

indicators.note: something embraced is held in the arms of another, so this piece sits within the next

parts.note: nude means without clothes
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German is hugged by an undressed young woman and given a little poke.
explanation.walkthrough: NUDE plus D makes NUDED, and G goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to push someone lightly, usually with the elbow, so nudged is a gentle prod in the past tense.

clue.text: Squirm when legal document's served to His Excellency

indicators.note: a thing served to someone is handed to them, so the first piece comes right before the second

parts.note: a writ is a written court order; the 's reads as 'is'
HE is the standard abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: An ambassador squirms when served with a writ.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and turn the body in pain or discomfort, which is to squirm.

clue.text: Special attention given to animal making nest for rook: something to keep it off the crops

definitions.text: something to keep it off the crops

indicators.note: a nest surrounds what lives in it, so the animal goes around the bird

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
to give care is to pay attention
a cow is a farm animal
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A farmer gives special attention to a beast and a nest, hoping to keep birds from the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside COW. The 'it' in the definition refers back to the rook, the bird the device is meant to scare.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a figure dressed as a person and set up in a field to frighten birds away from crops.

clue.text: Awfully bright leaders of Labour usually relapse in detox

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are those at the front, so take each word's opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A Labour politician, despite rehab, keeps falling back into bad habits in a garish way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid colours are unpleasantly vivid or glaring, so lurid means overly or horribly bright.

clue.text: So-called convert is part of the furniture in church

definitions.text: part of the furniture in church

indicators.note: so-called means named that way, signalling the word as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: to convert something is to change or alter it

explanation.surface: A so-called convert has become a fixture of the parish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of the furniture' is an idiom for someone always present, which misleads; here it is literal church furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The altar is the table at the east end of a church where communion is celebrated, a central church fitting.

clue.text: Capacity to endure hardship with no treacle, unfortunately!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it come out disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bears the hardship of an empty treacle tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the ability to put up with pain or difficulty, the capacity to endure.

clue.text: Typical example of drug and letter found by book

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A doctor's drug and a covering letter sit beside a textbook, a model case.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example of a type, the one that embodies its qualities.

clue.text: Setter to criticise a nasty city

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves is I
to slam is to criticise harshly
taken as written
bad means unpleasant or nasty

explanation.surface: The setter sets out to knock a disagreeable city.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: Little dog's favourite toy that dangles on a string

definitions.text: toy that dangles on a string

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A puppy's favourite plaything swings from a piece of string.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet is a figure worked by strings, a marionette, so it is a toy hanging from strings.

clue.text: Star with five points in enclosure identifying sign on animal

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
a tag is a label that identifies something
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A star-shaped ear tag identifies an animal kept in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star drawn with five straight strokes.

clue.text: Woman is happy to meet unknown son

parts.note: glad means pleased or happy
in algebra, x, y and z stand for unknowns
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother is delighted to meet the son she never knew.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a female first name, so it stands for a woman in crossword style.

clue.text: Fired ammunition at second home of 25 used by editor

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
25 is DEVIL, and the devil lives in hell
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor bombarded a second residence.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends the solver to 25-down, whose answer is DEVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell is to bombard with artillery shells, so shelled means fired ammunition at.

clue.text: Mr Stone destroyed fabulous beast

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters before it are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Stone has slain a legendary creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster is a mythical creature of fable, such as a dragon, so it is a fabulous beast.

clue.text: Water supply contaminated by silt finally gets a service

indicators.note: a thing contaminated has something foreign got into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the mains is the public water supply pipe

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the next word, so only its closing letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A dirty water supply gets a service from the plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like maintenance work on pipes; here it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins is the morning prayer service in the Anglican and Catholic churches.

clue.text: King and old saint on strange platform

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
O is the abbreviation for old
ST is the abbreviation for saint
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A king and an aged saint stand on an unfamiliar stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: On which to weigh bits of fish?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the small plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests weighing pieces of fish at the fishmonger's, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an instrument for weighing and the thin overlapping plates on a fish's body.

clue.text: Able to visit, carrying post to temporary shelter

indicators.note: a thing carrying another holds it within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to come round is to visit
P stands for post, as in p&p, postage and packing
a tent is a portable, temporary shelter

explanation.surface: A visitor brings the post to someone camping in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The post letter sits between the third and fourth letters of the visiting word, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent describes someone with enough skill to do a job, so it means capable or able.

clue.text: Specific thing used to chop up disembowelled convict

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an axe is a tool for chopping wood

indicators.note: a disembowelled body has lost its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of this word remain

explanation.surface: A specific weapon is used to hack up a gutted prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop up' reads as one verb, but 'up' belongs to the reversal and 'thing used to chop' is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise and particular, which is the sense of specific.

clue.text: Chief of Scandinavians going from first to third place in mountains

indicators.note: the chief of a group is its head, naming the leading letter as the one that will move

indicators.text: going from first to third place
indicators.note: a letter moving from the front to the third slot rearranges the word's letters

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark, a Scandinavian country

explanation.surface: A Nordic team leader slips from first to third in a mountain race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief of Scandinavians' is the D at the head of DANES; move it to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range running down the west of South America.

clue.text: Wretched creature died corrupt

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
evil means wicked or morally corrupt

explanation.surface: A miserable being has passed away, rotten to the core.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil is used of an unfortunate person, as in 'poor devil', so it can mean a wretched creature.

clue.text: Sign held by Bengali Brahman

indicators.note: held by means contained within the following words, running across their boundary

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Bengali priest of the highest caste holds up a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Vehicle in which to catch dog?

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A dog warden uses a van to round up a stray.
explanation.walkthrough: A Land Rover is a British four-wheel-drive off-road vehicle; the question mark flags the pun on its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land Rover is a make of rugged four-wheel-drive car, so it is a vehicle.

clue.text: Dead set on becoming awkward, so tranquillised

indicators.note: becoming awkward means turning clumsy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient determined to be difficult has been drugged into calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedated means given a calming drug, which is what being tranquillised is.

clue.text: Setter returned to British Library with retired setter's badge

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves is me
BL is the abbreviation for the British Library

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so this word too is read in reverse

parts.note: again the setter as me

explanation.surface: A retired setter goes back to the British Library wearing a badge.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbol or device worn as a sign of identity, the same idea as a badge.
